title: Lesson 20: Shadow IT: Discovering and Governing Unsanctioned AI
description: Grounded in Lesson 20 of the AI Adoption series: why banning unsanctioned AI pushes it underground rather than eliminating it, why shadow AI differs from classic shadow IT, and how a repeatable discover, triage, govern, repeat loop turns invisible usage into a governed inventory.

questions.question: Why does blocking an unsanctioned tool tend to raise risk rather than remove it?
options: Because blocked tools are usually replaced by more expensive ones
Because users find workarounds, keeping use outside your sight
Because blocking forces the vendor to raise its security posture
Because users stop processing data entirely until approval arrives
questions.explanation: Prohibition does not end the need the tool was meeting, so people route around the block and you lose the limited visibility you had.

questions.question: When triaging a discovered tool, what should drive the governance decision?
options: How much the tool costs and whether a budget line exists for it
Which department adopted it and how senior its sponsor is
What data the tool handles and whether that data may leave
How popular the tool is among staff who have tried it
questions.explanation: Triage is a data question, not a popularity or budget question: what category of data the tool sees, and whether that category may go to a provider you never vetted.

questions.question: Why pair a restriction on a risky tool with a sanctioned alternative?
options: Because a sanctioned tool is always cheaper than the one it replaces
Because blocking a tool is not permitted under most privacy laws
Because approved tools never need any review once they are listed
Because the underlying need remains after the tool is blocked
questions.explanation: A need does not disappear because the tool meeting it was removed, so giving people a safe path is what stops the workaround from reappearing ungoverned.
